title: stitch-handoff-notes-draft
content:
Purpose: quick, portable handoff template + scratchpad for emergent issues. Kept intentionally terse so next on-call can scan and act.

Summary from my shift (11/07 -> 11/08):
- Rolling upgrade of quantized kernels started at ~02:10 UTC. Canary instances (canary-pool-3) showed higher 95p latency for short sequences after the upgrade; rollback initiated at 02:42 UTC.
- Temporary mitigation: pinned affected nodes back to v2kernels-alpha until PR 2431 is vetted. See PR for kernel profiler logs.
- Two customer-facing errors surfaced (500s) tied to routing fallbacks hitting slow model-variants during autoscaling window. Impact ~3 minutes, ~12 requests.

Immediate priorities for next shift:
1) Verify pin is still in place on dedicated pools: kubectl get pods -l pool=dedicated-usw2 -o wide and check image tag (should be v2kernels-stable).
2) Confirm canary tests are green after today’s smoke (there was a flaky bench): run the smoke harness -> //tools/smoke/run_smoke.sh --canary canary-pool-3
3) Validate no regressions in the routing service: check trace sample in console -> route=fast-path, then open a few traces sampled at >200ms.

Hotfixes/Actions taken (chronological):
- 02:22 UTC: heatmap showed sudden spike in tail latency on canary batchers. Noted increased GC in python wrapper (gcmem).
- 02:30 UTC: scaled down canary batch size via runtime flag to reduce memory pressure (flag: BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512 -> 384).
- 02:42 UTC: rolled back kernel update (image -> v2kernels-stable). Observed latencies revert by ~02:50 UTC.
- 03:10 UTC: filed JIRA-1042 to track follow-up: kernel optimization + CI stress tests for short-seq workloads.

Ongoing / unresolved items:
- Root cause of GC spike unclear — may be interaction between new kernel memory alloc and python sidecar. Need heap profiles from runtime nodes (see linked PR where minimal profiles attached but not full sampling).
- Autoscaler edge-case where fallback models are slightly larger (ram) than primary fast-path variants; need to confirm fallback selection policy once more.

Temporary playbook (use this if more than one customer hits 5xxs):
1) Immediately set routing-policy to prefer fallback-tier 'stable-small' for incoming traffic: curl -X POST ${ROUTER_ADMIN}/policy --data '{"prefer":"stable-small"}' (note: use admin token from vault secret infra/router-admin).
2) If latency > 500ms for >5m, isolate new deployments: kubectl cordon <node-name> and scale down deployment to prior revision.
3) If errors persist, enable automatic fallback to hosted-api region (region-failover) by flipping feature-flag: /ops/flags/set region-failover=true. This will increase token cost but restore availability.

Deep-dive quick checklist (if you need to investigate):
- Check metrics: /grafana/d/redwood/runtime-overview?orgId=1 -> filter by pool and model-variant. Look at p50/p95/p99 and request counts.
- Logs: gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND labels.k8s-pod/app="serving-runtime"' --limit 1000 --project redwood-prod -> filter for OOM or allocation errors.
- Heap/profile: /ops/profiler/collect --pod=<pod> --duration=60s. If profiler fails, try tcpdump on host to see memory spikes.
- Trace: open a couple of traces in Console -> check for extra hops in smart-routing (sometimes the router queries KV cache twice).

Useful commands (copy-paste friendly):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
- kubectl logs -n redwood <pod> -c runtime --tail=500
- curl -s ${ROUTER_ADMIN}/health | jq
- /tools/smoke/run_smoke.sh --canary <canary_pool> --verbose

Dashboards & runbooks to reference:
- Runtime overview (grafana) -> /dashboards/runtime-overview
- Routing & fallbacks -> confluence:CONFLUENCE-9876
- Autoscaler tuning notes -> confluence:AUTO-TUNING-2

Escalation contacts (order):
1) Ravi Kapoor (infra lead) - slack @ravi - pager (primary)
2) Maya Thompson (runtime eng) - slack @maya - pager (secondary)
3) On-call PM (rotation) - see /ops/oncall-calendar for name

Notes to self (short):
- When checking PR 2431, pay attention to the microbench harness for seq len 8 and batch size 1 — that's where the regression showed up.
- Add an assertion to CI that simulates KV cache warmup when kernel changes are introduced.
- Remember to update the 'rollback playbook' with the new image tag pattern we used tonight.

Open questions / follow-ups for engineering:
- Is there a memory accounting mismatch between kernel alloc and python profiler? (Maya to investigate)
- Should routing fallback prefer smaller-memory variants even if slightly slower to avoid OOM cascades? (Design decision, log in JIRA-1042)

Short TODOs for next shift (priority sorted):
- [ ] Confirm rollback pin still on dedicated pools (5m).
- [ ] Run targeted smoke on short sequences (10m).
- [ ] Upload heap profiles to JIRA ticket and annotate.
- [ ] Ping infra slack channel with incident summary and link to this file.

Misc scratch notes / shorthand (delete when finalized):
- "stitch" = quick concatenation of runbook pieces for fast handoff. Keep this file short and noisy.
- If you see repeated router->kv double-reads, try disabling async-cache = true temporarily.
- Contact list is stale? check /ops/contacts and update this doc.

End of notes. If you are coming on shift: skim "Immediate priorities" and run the two commands under "Useful commands" first. If anything is urgent, @ravi and @maya are the fastest path.

-- Avery
